subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make non-sandboxed agents workspace-confined by default, or keep host-wide file access as an explicit trusted-local capability with opt-in sandbox/tool policy?
rationale: The code can enforce either shape, but changing defaults affects existing workflows and the security trust model, and file-tool confinement alone does not cover exec/process access.

options.title: Adopt a staged confinement plan
options.body: Define a compatibility-aware default policy, land narrow hardening where safe, and keep this issue open until file tools and exec/sandbox docs match the chosen boundary.

options.title: Keep opt-in host access
options.body: Maintain the current trusted-local default and resolve this as documentation/support only after explicitly accepting the security tradeoff.

options.title: Flip filesystem tools first
options.body: Default `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` or equivalent enforcement to on, with migration/docs, while tracking exec/process isolation separately.

recommendation.title: Adopt a staged confinement plan
recommendation.body: Define a compatibility-aware default policy, land narrow hardening where safe, and keep this issue open until file tools and exec/sandbox docs match the chosen boundary.
